messages:
eli_customer: Hi support — heads up: we’re seeing a reproducible problem with streaming (SSE) where sessions run for a couple minutes, then suddenly emit a 429 mid-stream and close. Clients get partial output and users are being billed for the whole session plus the resumed session. This is affecting ~12% of streams for AcornHealth right now.

eli_customer: Minimal repro attached below (curl). Also seeing this on mobile where reconnects are common. Billing shows tokens charged twice for the same logical session id. Can we triage?

lina_support: Sorry you hit this — we’ll escalate. Can you paste the exact request headers and a snippet of the SSE output you get when it fails? Also your account id and a couple example request ids if available.

eli_customer: Account: acorn-prod-42. Example request id (root): req_0a1b2c3d. Headers:
```
Authorization: Bearer sk-acorn-xxxxx
Accept: text/event-stream
Content-Type: application/json
X-Session-Id: acorn-12345
User-Agent: AcornMobile/4.2.1
```
SSE output (trimmed):
```
data: {"id":"msg_001","type":"partial","text":"Patient record: Jane Doe..."}

data: {"id":"msg_002","type":"partial","text":"Medications: metformin..."}

event: error
data: {"code":429,"message":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":5}
```
Connection closes right after the error. We then try to reconnect with same X-Session-Id and client-side resume=true and get continued tokens billed.

julia_sre: Thanks, adding SRE. I pulled the API logs for req_0a1b2c3d and nearby requests. I can see our rate-limiter returning a 429 about ~140s into the stream. Notable: the stream handler records billed tokens on initial allocation and again when a resume handshake is accepted. Looks like resume path increments the session ledger before checking for prior ledger entries -> potential double-charge.

julia_sre: snippet from our internal logs for that session (anonymized):
```
2026-03-15T10:02:12Z svc.streams INFO session_start session=acorn-12345 alloc_tokens=320
2026-03-15T10:04:34Z svc.streams WARN rate_limiter 429 session=acorn-12345 window_key=acct-acorn-prod-42
2026-03-15T10:04:35Z svc.streams INFO client_reconnect resume=true session=acorn-12345 alloc_tokens=320
2026-03-15T10:04:35Z svc.billing INFO ledger_increment session=acorn-12345 delta=320 (reason=resume)
2026-03-15T10:04:35Z svc.billing INFO ledger_increment session=acorn-12345 delta=320 (reason=initial)
```
The double ledger_increment is the smoking gun.

marta_eng: I can reproduce locally with a short script that simulates flaky mobile connections and immediate resume. The bug is in billing/session reconciliation: when a reconnect with resume=true is accepted, we re-apply the initial allocation without checking if it was already applied earlier for the same server-side session nonce. On high-latency or partial-send cases, the rate limiter may reject mid-stream and the client resumes — we then charge again.

marta_eng: Proposed fix: change resume path to consult the session_ledger first and only apply delta = max(0, desired_alloc - ledger.current_alloc). Also add instrumentation to detect duplicate increments and emit an alert. I have a branch with tests.

kevin_billing: If that’s accurate we should proactively issue credits for affected accounts. How long would a fix take and can we do a hotfix for production? We need a list of impacted sessions for reconciliation.

julia_sre: I’ll dump the query to enumerate sessions where ledger shows two identical increments within 10s and the same session id. That should identify duplicates.

omar_beckett: Can you paste a small repro script for customers to run so we can verify? I’ll use it to test the patch during canary.

marta_eng: Sure — Node snippet below (super small, intentionally flaky):
```
// resume-repro.js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
async function start() {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': 'Bearer sk-acorn-xxxxx',
      'Accept': 'text/event-stream',
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'X-Session-Id': 'acorn-12345'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({model:'redwood-1', input: 'long prompt...', resume: false})
  });
  // read a couple events then forcibly close to simulate flaky network
  const reader = res.body.getReader();
  let {value} = await reader.read();
  process.stdout.write(new TextDecoder().decode(value));
  reader.cancel(); // abrupt close
  // immediately reconnect with resume
  await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?resume=true', {method: 'POST', headers: {/* same headers incl. X-Session-Id */}});
}
start();
```
marta_eng: Running this against current prod reproduces the double-charge path consistently.

eli_customer: We ran the script in prod and reproduced. On mobile we see retries ~70% of the time when signal toggles; each reconnect seems to register additional billed tokens.

julia_sre: Short-term mitigation: if customers include an explicit X-Client-Resume header with a monotonic resume_counter we can avoid accidental double-allocations on our end while we patch. We’ll also throttle immediate reconnects from same IP/session for 2s to reduce duplicate ledger writes.

marta_eng: I opened PR #4127 with the ledger-safe-resume change + unit tests. Plan: canary to 10% of traffic in us-east after 1 hour of smoke tests. If smoke looks good roll to 100% in 2 hours.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary/ledger-safe-resume -> us-east-1 at 2026-03-15T13:15:00Z (sha: c3f4b2).

kevin_billing: I’ll prepare a credit runbook and export the impacted session list once julia posts the query. We should credit full duplicate increments for affected accounts and communicate.

lina_support: I’ll draft a targeted message to AcornHealth (priority) explaining cause and ETA for fix and credits.

omar_beckett: Quick QA checklist for canary: run resume-repro.js 50x against canary endpoint, assert ledger increments only once, assert no 429 midstream due to rate-limiter thrash (we still expect legitimate 429s when quota exceeds defined limits).

eli_customer: Thanks everyone — appreciate the rapid triage. Please cc me on the credit and fix updates. I’ll hold clients until the fix is confirmed.

julia_sre: Will follow up with the impacted session query and results in this thread. ETA 30–45m. For now, workaround: set X-Client-Resume: <monotonic-integer> and prefer short backoff before resume.

marta_eng: After canary we’ll patch billing reconciliation to run a nightly reconcilier to auto-fix past double-charges if any slipped through.

eli_customer: Received, thanks :pray:
